courses.title: Introduction to International Relations and Diplomacy
courses.description: This course aims to provide students with the analytical skills and critical knowledge to understand key concepts, principles and cases relating to international relations (IR) and diplomatic affairs. Students will be introduced to different kinds of literature, to make them familiar with the actors, goals, means, and consequences of state interaction in the field of international relations. This course will also explore a number of theoretical debates in diplomatic studies, and the practice of global diplomacy with a particular focus on its applicability in the contemporary world order.
courses.course_syllabus:
Week 1: Introduction to international relations and diplomacy
This session will introduce a brief history of international relations and diplomacy in our global world. We will answer questions such as ‘Why do we have various different theories of international relations?’ and ‘What is diplomacy?’.

Week 2: The rise of modern international order and global diplomacy
This session will examine the emergence of international orders and different theoretical approaches to international relations and apply various concepts to the practice of diplomacy. We will also discuss the relationship between great and small powers in international relations and global diplomacy.

Week 3: Actors in international affairs and diplomacy
This session will focus on different actors in international relations and diplomacy. We will also discuss the complexity of contemporary international relations and the changing international environment that formulate foreign policies.

Week 4: International organizations in international affairs: The United Nations
This session will analyse the powers of the UN Security Council and General Assembly to authorize the use of force and non-military sanctions in international relations.

Week 5: Bilateral and Multilateral Diplomacy
This session will discuss how bilateral and multilateral diplomacy today deals with the full range of international issues: war and peace, human rights, trade, the environment, etc.

Week 6: International issues: Trade and diplomacy
This session will discuss different forms of trade disputes in international politics and how conflict can be peacefully settled. These include the operating conditions of diplomacy and the WTO’s dispute settlement mechanism in our global world.

Week 7: International issues: War and diplomacy
This session discusses what war is, and how it affects societies and politics in international relations. This session also highlights the importance of diplomacy in modern states, armed forces and wars.

Week 8: International issues: Environment and international relations
This session will examine environmental issues in international relations and politics since 1945. We will also discuss the problems and challenges faced by global governance in solving environmental problems from different perspectives.

Week 9: Human rights, individuals and cultural diplomacy in international relations
This session will focus on human rights, individuals and people to people exchange. We will also consider if there are universal human rights in our global world.

Week 10: Guest talk
A guest speaker will be invited to share with our students on the current issues related to international relations and diplomacy.

Week 11: Group presentations and discussions
Group presentations on selected topics with Q&A sessions.

Week 12: The future of international relations and diplomacy
This course will examine the role that artificial intelligence plays in disrupting and shaping the future of our global politics and international law.

Week 13: Conclusion & end of term essay prep
This course will end with an account of the problems and prospects of international relations and diplomacy.

courses.subject: DIPL
courses.title: Introduction to International Conflicts and Sanctions
courses.description: This course aims to teach the causes and consequences of international conflicts among nations. In particular, economic sanctions are one of the most popular mechanisms that are used to respond to security challenges. The course will begin with a foundational review of international conflicts and wars. The second part will examine how sanctions are designed and managed as a foreign policy tool. This course will provide an introduction to key debates and practices of policies on international sanctions and discuss the concept and evolution of international sanctions and their role in international conflicts.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to

1. critically analyze the basic forces that shape international conflicts;
2. be familiar with the formulation of sanction policies; and
3. analyze different theories and arguments in the sphere of economic sanctions.
courses.course_syllabus:
Week 1: Introduction to international conflicts and sanctions
This session will examine the origins of major international conflicts. In particular, what is the geopolitical view of the distribution of power among states and what are international conflicts. This session will also discuss different types of economic sanctions and their political contexts.

Week 2: Interactions, deterrence and escalation of international conflicts
This session will discuss how deterrence has emerged as the primary resource relied on by the superpowers during the Cold War. This session will also examine how deterrence was developed and employed primarily to prevent escalation with some successful and failed cases.

Week 3: Why are sanctions imposed in international conflicts
This session will focus on who the key actors are and why sanctions are imposed in terms of the policy objectives pursued. This session will also examine the course, organization and expectations of sanctions and how the impact of sanctions can be evaluated.

Week 4: The UN approach to sanctions
This session will analyse the use of targeted sanctions by the UN Security Council (UNSC) and the transformation of the use of sanctions by the UN. Some international cases will be discussed.

Week 5: The US approach to sanctions
This session will discuss how the US today deals with the full range of sanctions and why the US uses sanctions much more frequently than other countries since the Second World War.

Week 6: China and Russia's use of sanctions
This session will discuss how China and Russia (the former Soviet Union) deal with sanctions. Some major cases will be evaluated.

Week 7: The EU approach to sanctions
This session will provide an overview of EU sanctions, why they are imposed, what they do and who must comply. This session will also focus on the legal framework governing sanctions, guidance provided by the European Commission and the role of EU Member States in implementing and enforcing sanctions.

Week 8: Case study: International sanctions against Iran
This session will focus on the international sanctions against Iran and the scope and impact of sanctions on society, economy and politics in Iran.

Week 9: Case study: Case study: International sanctions against Russia
This session will focus on the international sanctions against Russia and the scope and impact of sanctions on society, economy and politics in Russia.

Week 10: Alternatives of sanctions in solving international conflicts
This session will examine the impact of sanctions on our global political economy and discuss any alternatives to economic sanctions in solving international conflicts.

Week 11: Group presentations and discussions
Group presentations on selected topics with Q&A sessions.

Week 12: The future of sanctions and international conflicts
This course will examine the role of sanctions in international conflicts and how international sanctions will shape the future of our global political economy.

Week 13: Conclusion & end of term essay prep
This course will end with an account of the problems and prospects of international conflicts and sanctions.
